Approved findings

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

CrowdTruth 2.0: Quality Metrics for Crowdsourcing with Disagreement (1808.06080v1) · paper method: Worker, media-unit and annotation quality are mutually dependent scores initialized to one and repeatedly recalculated until their total variation falls below a chosen threshold; the reported formulation uses disagreement-weighted cosine agreement.

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

CrowdTruth 2.0: Quality Metrics for Crowdsourcing with Disagreement (1808.06080v1) · paper method: For open-ended tasks, annotation quality cannot be calculated across multiple media units and is set to one; the paper describes further comparative validation across tasks as future work, so the formulas alone do not establish measured improvement on a new task.

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

CrowdTruth 2.0: Quality Metrics for Crowdsourcing with Disagreement (1808.06080v1) · paper method: CrowdTruth 2.0 represents each worker response as a binary annotation vector; a closed task shares a predefined answer space, while an open task forms its media-unit-specific answer space from the unique worker-provided keywords.

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

CrowdTruth 2.0: Quality Metrics for Crowdsourcing with Disagreement (1808.06080v1) · paper method: The defined worker-quality score is the product of worker–worker agreement and worker–media-unit agreement, so individual-peer consistency and agreement with the aggregate of other workers both contribute; the paper presents definitions rather than a new controlled accuracy result.
